subject: Approval needed: Onboarding email sequence v1 (tone + claims) for Lifecycle Sprint launch
body:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tyler Benson <tyler.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 13, 2025 at 9:14 AM PT
Subject: Approval needed: Onboarding email sequence v1 (tone + claims) for Lifecycle Sprint launch

Camila, Soojin —

We’re queued to launch the 5-email onboarding sequence as part of the Lifecycle Growth Experiments Sprint (Week 1 launch). I need final sign-off on:

1) Tone (developer-first, not salesy)
2) Claims (benchmarks/latency/cost language) + any required substantiation links

Doc (comments enabled):
- Google Drive: onboarding-email-copy-v1

A few specific points to review:
- Email #2 subject line variant: “First successful call in 5 minutes (copy/paste)” — does “5 minutes” feel too absolute?
- Email #3 includes: “Cut inference latency + cost without changing your prompts” — we can soften if needed.
- Retargeting + email copy references “Redwood-verified performance profiles” (from our messaging pillars) — OK to keep?

If we can get approval by EOD Tue, Tyler can lock the final UTM/campaign naming and we can schedule sends.

Attached is a PDF snapshot for quick review if that’s easier.

Thanks,
Ben

Ben Carter
Growth Marketing — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Onboarding_Emails_v1_for_Approval.pdf

---

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tyler Benson <tyler.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 13, 2025 at 10:02 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval needed: Onboarding email sequence v1 (tone + claims) for Lifecycle Sprint launch

Thanks Ben.

A few quick flags after reading through:

- “First successful call in 5 minutes” reads like a promise. I’d recommend “in a few minutes” or “in minutes” unless we have a published guarantee.
- “Cut inference latency + cost without changing your prompts” is directionally true, but it implies automatic improvements. Can we rewrite to “Explore levers to reduce latency and cost…”?
- Any “X% faster” / “cheaper than” comparisons: I didn’t see explicit numbers (good), but I want to ensure we’re only making claims we can back up with a public link.

If we want to keep “Redwood-verified performance profiles,” I’d add a link to the relevant docs page (or a public blog post) in the footer. Otherwise we should use softer wording like “curated performance profiles.”

I left a few line-level comments in the doc.

Soojin

---

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tyler Benson <tyler.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 13, 2025 at 10:18 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval needed: Onboarding email sequence v1 (tone + claims) for Lifecycle Sprint launch

+1 to Soojin’s notes.

Two additional exec-level concerns:

1) Make sure these emails don’t read like they’re for enterprises. Keep it squarely self-serve devs (“copy/paste curl,” “SDK snippet,” “common errors”) and avoid anything that sounds like we’re upselling Dedicated/Private.

2) Please add a clear line somewhere (footer is fine) about managing email preferences. We don’t need to overdo it, but I want it explicit.

Otherwise the structure looks good.

Camila

Camila Reyes
VP Marketing — Redwood Inference

---

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tyler Benson <tyler.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 13, 2025 at 12:06 PM PT
Subject: Re: Approval needed: Onboarding email sequence v1 (tone + claims) for Lifecycle Sprint launch

Got it — thank you both.

Proposed edits (I can turn these around today):

- Subject line: change “First successful call in 5 minutes” -> “First successful call in minutes”
- Rewrite the “Cut latency + cost…” line to: “See the main levers to reduce latency and unit cost (batching, caching, streaming) — no prompt rewrite required to get started.”
- Replace “Redwood-verified performance profiles” -> “curated performance profiles” in body copy, and keep “verified” only if we can link to a public doc.
- Add footer line in every email: “Manage your email preferences / unsubscribe” (Tyler: will your tooling insert the standard footer automatically, or do you want us to include it in copy?)

Soojin — for substantiation links, can we point to the docs quickstart + a public benchmarks page (if available), rather than anything that could be interpreted as a competitive claim?

I’ll ping Ethan separately in case we need a specific “proof point” link.

Ben

---

From: Tyler Benson <tyler.benson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 13, 2025 at 12:24 PM PT
Subject: Re: Approval needed: Onboarding email sequence v1 (tone + claims) for Lifecycle Sprint launch

Ben — our sending platform will append the standard unsubscribe footer automatically, but I’d still include a short “update preferences” line in-body for clarity (especially given the suppression-rule workstream).

Also: please avoid hard-coded console URLs in the body if possible. Use the shortlink format so we can swap paths if routing changes (SUP-2841 risk).

Tyler

---

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Wallace <ethan.wallace@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 13, 2025 at 1:01 PM PT
Subject: Quick check: public link we can use for “performance profiles” / benchmarking mention?

Ethan —

Do we have a public-safe doc/blog link that supports any of the following (without turning into a competitive claim)?

- “curated performance profiles” / “verified performance profiles” language
- “production-grade inference: latency/cost/reliability” (qualitative is fine)

We can also keep it entirely qualitative, but Soojin asked to ensure anything that reads like a claim has a link.

Need by tomorrow AM if possible.

Ben

---

From: Ethan Wallace <ethan.wallace@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Jan 13, 2025 at 2:37 PM PT
Subject: Re: Quick check: public link we can use for “performance profiles” / benchmarking mention?

Yes — use the docs page that explains model catalog + runtime behavior (no competitor comparisons) and the “how we measure latency/cost” blog post.

I’ll DM you the exact links I’m comfortable with, but guidance:
- Avoid “verified” unless we define what verified means (e.g., “benchmarked by Redwood on listed hardware”).
- “Curated performance profiles” is safe.

Ethan

---

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tyler Benson <tyler.benson@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Wallace <ethan.wallace@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 9:46 AM PT
Subject: Re: Approval needed: Onboarding email sequence v1 (tone + claims) for Lifecycle Sprint launch

Update: I pushed revisions in the doc (resolved most comments).

Summary of changes:
- Removed “5 minutes” promise. Now: “First successful call in minutes” / “copy/paste and run.”
- Reframed latency/cost line to “levers to reduce latency and unit cost” (no guarantee language).
- Swapped “Redwood-verified performance profiles” -> “curated performance profiles.”
- Replaced hard-coded console paths with shortlinks (per Tyler).
- Added an in-body “Manage email preferences” line (footer still auto-appended).
- Added one “Learn more” link to the public-safe explainer Ethan recommended (no competitive language).

Camila/Soojin — if you’re comfortable, can you reply-all with an explicit “approved to send” so I can lock copy and schedule? Targeting first send tomorrow morning.

Ben

Subject: Re: Approval needed: Onboarding email sequence v1 (tone + claims) for Lifecycle Sprint launch

Reviewed — approved to send.

Thanks for softening the language and adding the substantiation link.

Soojin

Ben — please make sure we monitor unsubscribes/support volume in the first 24 hours and post a quick check-in in #marketing + #support.

Camila
